builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TQIR: Trellis Quantization with Integer Reconstruction for Bandwidth-Efficient Edge LLM Acceleration
summary: TQIR replaces floating-point trellis weight decoding with offline trellis matching constrained to exact INT8/INT4 codewords, enabling integer GEMM with reduced weight-memory traffic, and moves the reverse Hadamard transform to the activation side. It requires algorithm-hardware co-design, including a custom decoder block, subspace Hadamard transform, and compatible integer-GEMM runtime, so adoption costs implementation complexity beyond a typical software-only quantization workflow. It can fail for teams without custom silicon or specialized kernel support, and gains may not transfer if model accuracy, memory bandwidth, or deployment hardware differ from the evaluated setting.
rationale: The method targets bandwidth reduction and integer inference, but its claimed benefit depends on custom hardware support that a constrained single-GPU or API-based practitioner cannot directly deploy.
technique: Trellis quantization with integer reconstruction for edge LLMs

It requires algorithm-hardware co-design, including a custom decoder block, subspace Hadamard transform, and compatible integer-GEMM runtime, so adoption costs implementation complexity beyond a typical software-only quantization workflow. Configurable decoder delivers 307.2 Gweights/s in 0.0509 mm^2, achieving 13.93x and 1.52x the normalized decoder-area efficiency of Ecco and Codeword Decomposition.
